title: chat.moderation_content
description: A message's content, for an external moderation module's screening and moderator card. Identifiers travel on the bus; the content is fetched by this call at the moment it is looked at, so a case opened hours ago shows the message as it is now, edits included. A moderation policy names this function as its `content_function` for the `chat_message` target type (see stapel_chat/moderation.py). Response: {"text", "title", "language", "media", "author_id", "url", "kind", "conversation_id", "conversation_kind", "scope_key", "seq", "edited", "created_at"} — a conversation has no title and a message no declared language or public URL, so those come back empty rather than invented; `media` carries the attachment KEYS (opaque CDN handles, not bytes). A deleted or erased message raises a LookupError: a tombstone is gone, not empty, and a blank card is indistinguishable from a message that said nothing. Unguarded by design: who may read a case's content is the moderation module's `can_view_content` policy to answer.

message_id.description: The moderation case's `target_key` for a `chat_message` target: either a bare message id, or the composite `<conversation_id>:<message_id>` a composite uses so that WHO may report a message is answerable off its own conversation table. Given the composite form both halves must agree, or the message is not this target.
